title: Uniformity of Consistency in Arithmetic and Gödel's Second Incompleteness Theorem: Ein Märchen
summary: In much discussed work Artemov has recently argued that, for $\mathrm{PA}$, the consistency schema admits a form of uniform verification via selector-proofs, despite the unprovability of the corresponding uniform consistency sentence $\mathrm{Con}(\mathrm{PA})$. In this note, we show that this phenomenon extends to all sufficiently strong, uniformly reflexive arithmetizable theories, including $\mathrm{ZF}$ and many of their extensions: For such theories $T$, there exists a primitive recursive selector which, given a derivation code $d$, extracts a finite fragment $T_d\subseteq T$ containing…
